title: vl02: the norm of (1/sqrt j) is said to grow logarithmically; it is the partial sums of the squared moduli

legacy.new_text: Die Teilsummen der Betragsquadrate von $\vb{u}$ wachsen also wie ein Logarithmus über alle Grenzen.
The partial sums of the squared moduli of $\vb{u}$ thus grow beyond all bounds, like a logarithm.

reason: vl02.tex:133-136 say that for v_j = 1/sqrt(j) and f(x) = 1/sqrt(1+|x|) 'die Norm aber logarithmisch gegen unendlich' geht. What grows like a logarithm is the partial sum of the squared moduli, sum_{j<=N} 1/j >= ln(N+1) (and the partial integral 2 ln(1+X)); the truncated norm is its square root and grows like the square root of a logarithm. Moreover the norm is not yet defined in vl02 (it is vl03 material). The new chapter states the bound for the squared quantities (c03.eq.rate, c03.eq.log) and does not use the word norm.

evidence.independent_check: evidence/derivations/c03/check_c03.py verifies H_N >= ln(N+1) for N = 1..25 and int_0^X dx/(1+x) = ln(1+X) symbolically
